label: GO step, choosing a1 just after a reward, early in the episode (fades over a reward streak)
explanation: Fires only at GO (never at D1/D2), only when the previous trial was rewarded (prev_reward==1), and only when the agent picks a1 (model_act==1; 99.9% of mass, policy logit a1-a2 > 8). It never fires on a2 choices or after unrewarded trials. Within an episode it is strongest early and fades out: none after about trial 75. Magnitude peaks (~1.0) on the first rewarded trial after an unrewarded one and drops over consecutive rewards (roughly 1.0, 0.7, 0.45, 0.26 in example streaks), so it acts like a reward-surprise / win-stay-on-a1 signal that habituates. The recorded predicate keeps only GO steps where the reward run is at most 2 trials long (or the history is outside the window). All variables in it are observable or are the agent own choice. Dev: P 0.46, R 0.88, F1 0.60, mass recall 0.95. The simpler GO & prev_reward==1 & a1 & ep_trial<70 gets R 0.99 / P 0.38. Precision stays limited because many rewarded a1 GO steps in long streaks or later in the episode do not fire, and a fixed streak cutoff does not fully capture the decay.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=GO & last=a1 S2 r (+2.98), last=a1 S2 r (+2.60), phase=GO & before=a1 S2 u (+2.53), model_act=1 (+2.33), choice_bin=decile 9 (9 = most a1) (+2.33), phase=GO & choice_bin=decile 9 (9 = most a1) (+2.33). Lower it: phase=GO & value_bin=decile 2 (9 = highest) (-4.52), model_act=0 (-3.79), last=a1 S2 u (-3.76), phase=GO & last=a1 S2 u (-3.73).
